subject: Shortfall protection request and concurrency surcharge waiver
messages:
From: Alex Hsu <alex.hsu@brightcart.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: PO Team <poteam@brightcart.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Shortfall protection request and concurrency surcharge waiver

Kimberly —

Quick note from my side: we have a product launch next Tuesday and our early telemetry shows a much higher QPS than we forecasted. Engineering expects a three-day 6–8x peak from 3/30–4/1 (mostly daytime US hours). We may exhaust our current concurrency headroom and hit overrun charges.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provision a temporary concurrency lift for that 72-hour window? Ideally a soft buffer we can burst into without immediate surcharge while we normalize traffic.
2) If there are overrun charges, can you apply a waiver or a reduced rate/credit for that launch window? We're a mid-stage account and this launch is strategic — it would help if we could get a short-term repricing or credit.

Attached: our internal launch forecast (summary). I can share the exact QPS numbers if you need them.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product, BrightCart
alex.hsu@brightcart.com

Attachment: brightcart_launch_forecast.pdf (summary)

Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Shortfall protection request and concurrency surcharge waiver

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch. We can support a short-term buffer but I need a couple of quick details to scope it and confirm pricing:
- Expected peak QPS (or tokens/min) and daily volume over the 3 days
- Whether this will be sustained across multiple regions or concentrated in us-west/us-east
- Any hard SLA requirement (e.g., 95th percentile latency target) during the spike

Commercially, we have two levers: a provisional concurrency uplift (timeboxed) and a blended overrun concession for the first week post-launch. To move fast I can prepare a temporary pricing proposal (terms + credit) if you can send the QPS numbers by EOD. I will loop Jordan (commercial) for approval and Ben for billing/PO runbook.

I'll draft a short proposal and upload it for signature once we agree the numbers. If helpful, we can also set a simple auto-fallback to a lower-cost model variant to limit spend.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

- Approve a timeboxed concurrency uplift for 2026-03-30 00:00 UTC through 2026-04-01 23:59 UTC. Recommend setting buffer = 2x their current headroom or up to 10k tokens/min, whichever is smaller.

Ben — can finance approve the 20% uplift concession + a discretionary $X credit cap? Also confirm whether tech needs additional runbook for enabling immediate fallback if traffic continues beyond the window.

Thanks for the quick follow. Based on the numbers you sent over in the launch forecast attachment, we've agreed internally to the following provisional plan:

What we'll enable
- Timeboxed concurrency buffer from 2026-03-30 00:00 UTC to 2026-04-01 23:59 UTC (72 hours). Buffer size: up to 10k tokens/min or 2x your current headroom, whichever you hit first.

Pricing & credits
- Overrun charges during the 72-hour window will be billed at our standard overrun rate but we'll apply a 20% credit to those charges (reflected on the invoice).
- If you escalate any billing discrepancies within 30 days with matching telemetry, we'll provision a discretionary credit while we reconcile.

Next steps / action items
1) Please countersign the attached temporary addendum ("temp_pricing_proposal.pdf") via DocuSign link below so we have formal approval to flip the switch.
2) PO Team: if you can send the PO number, we can attach it to the addendum and expedite billing reconciliation.
3) Tech ops (cc'd): will prepare the runbook and monitor the window; if traffic remains elevated after 72 hours we'll auto-fallback to agreed model variants to cap cost.
